verdict.rationale: Obsidian's docs say notes are stored as non-proprietary plain-text Markdown files on the local device, editable in other editors, so users can switch apps easily. Users independently confirm that the plain-text files can outlive Obsidian, and Canvas uses JSON files; one user's worry about a trend away from Markdown is not a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: a documented spec for the JSON (.canvas) format and Obsidian-specific syntax in the pack, and default wikilinks are non-standard Markdown unless switched off.

support.subject: As a researcher, my notes are stored or exportable in open, documented formats (Markdown, JSON) so my archive outlives the vendor

citations.quote: Obsidian stores your notes as Markdown-formatted plain text files in a vault.
Apps come and go, but your data should last. Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device.
Because notes are plain text files, you can use other text editors and file managers to edit and manage notes.
If interoperability is important to you, you can disable Wikilinks and use Markdown links instead.
